title: The Ninety-Fifth Quarter to the Bunker: the Comedian Who Played the President and Then Was One
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, the birth in the iron city
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The exact hospital is not named in any reachable source; the pin is city-centre Kryvyi Rih, an ore town strung out for more than a hundred kilometres along the Inhulets.
stops.campa: In the long ore town laid out along the Inhulets, pit after pit and slag heap after blast furnace, a son is born to Oleksandr Zelenskyy, who teaches computing and cybernetics, and to Rymma, an engineer. The family is Jewish. The grandfather came back from the war in a Red Army uniform and three of his brothers did not come back at all. Kryvyi Rih speaks Russian, mines iron, and has produced no presidents. They name the boy Volodymyr and enter him in the city register on the twenty-fifth of January.
suggested_refs: The Soviet-era residential quarters of Kryvyi Rih, numbered rather than named

stops.name: Erdenet, the copper town on the steppe
stops.date_confidence: attested as fact, approximate as to years. Wikipedia states he spent four years in Erdenet before starting elementary school; Soviet schooling began at seven, so the residence falls roughly 1981 to 1985. A supplied research note dating it to 1978 conflates it with his birth year and is rejected. Coordinates corrected to the Wikipedia figures for Erdenet; a figure of 49.0333 / 104.0833 circulating in the same note sits about three kilometres east of the town.
stops.campa: Before he is old enough for school the family moves to Erdenet, a town the Soviet Union built out of nothing in northern Mongolia around a copper and molybdenum pit and staffed with engineers shipped in from across the union. Oleksandr works the mining combine. For four years the boy's world is a Russian-language company town on the Mongolian steppe, several thousand kilometres of rail from the Inhulets, with Cyrillic street signs and no Ukrainian in it at all. Then the family goes home so that he can start first grade in Kryvyi Rih.
suggested_refs: The Erdenet Mining Corporation, the joint Mongolian-Soviet copper combine
sources: Reuters and Time profiles of Zelenskyy's childhood

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, the quarter that gives its number away
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 95th quarter as the family's district and as the source of the troupe's name is reported consistently in the Ukrainian press but the block itself is not given precise coordinates in any reachable source; the pin is approximate to the Ternivskyi district. The date is the notional start of first grade, used to order the segment.
stops.campa: The family settles in the residential blocks that Kryvyi Rih numbers rather than names, and the number of theirs is ninety-five. He will carry the number out with him. The troupe he founds takes it for a name, the studio that grows out of the troupe keeps it, and the Ukrainian corporate registry lists it still. What it names is an ordinary Soviet quarter of concrete slabs and a courtyard, with a school in which the language of instruction is Russian and boys who know one another from the stairwell.
suggested_refs: Kvartal 95, the residential block in Kryvyi Rih that names the studio
sources: Ukrainian press profiles of Kvartal 95's origin (Ukrayinska Pravda, Novoye Vremya)

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, the grant to Israel refused
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the fact and to his age; the month is not recorded and is set to June to order the segment. The law degree mentioned in the campa is dated 2000 and is folded into this stop rather than given its own.
stops.campa: At sixteen he sits the TOEFL, passes it, and wins a grant to study in Israel. His father says no. There is no record of an appeal and none of a second attempt. Twenty-eight years on he will address the Knesset by video link, an elected head of state speaking from a country under invasion. For now he stays in Kryvyi Rih and enrols at the local economic institute, a branch of the Kyiv national economics university. In 2000 he collects a law degree. He never uses it in a courtroom or anywhere else.
suggested_refs: The Kryvyi Rih Economic Institute, law faculty, now part of Kryvyi Rih National University

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, seventeen and into KVN
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; no month recorded, defaulted to January.
stops.campa: At seventeen he joins the local KVN team. The Klub Vesyolykh i Nakhodchivykh is a Soviet invention that outlived the Soviet Union: student troupes write, rehearse and perform sketch comedy against one another before judges and a national television audience, league by league, season by season. He starts as dance director, becomes a writer, then the man standing at the front. The team is called Zaporizhzhia-Kryvyi Rih-Transit and it is good enough to climb out of the provincial leagues into the circuit whose games are played and broadcast from Moscow.
suggested_refs: KVN, the televised comedy league, and its post-Soviet Moscow management

stops.name: Moscow, the Higher League title
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the month of the final is not recorded here and is set to June. Coordinates are the Moscow Palace of Youth on Komsomolsky Prospekt, where Higher League games were staged. A supplied research note placing the team in the Premier League at the MSU Palace of Culture on Sparrow Hills is rejected on two counts: the Premier League is a junior league Transit did not play, and the Sparrow Hills pin is about three and a half kilometres off.
stops.campa: Transit reaches the Higher League and wins the championship outright, sharing the title with an Armenian team. The stage is in Moscow, the judges are Russian, the broadcast is Russian, and so is the language of the jokes, because that is what a career in comedy means for a Ukrainian in the decade after the union dissolves. The league that has just crowned him will spend the next six years trying to buy his troupe away from him. He is nineteen years old.
suggested_refs: The Moscow Palace of Youth, home stage of the KVN Higher League

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, the troupe takes the quarter's name
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the month is not recorded and is set to September. The pin is the 95th quarter, approximate as above.
stops.campa: He and part of the Transit team break away to form their own troupe and name it after the block he grew up in: Kvartal 95. The ownership stays with the performers instead of going to a producer, which is not how that industry is arranged and which is the thing Moscow will object to. They write their own material and take it out on tour, through Ukraine, through Russia, through the Russian-speaking republics beyond, playing halls booked a season at a time.
suggested_refs: Kvartal 95 as a performing troupe, 1997 to 2003, before incorporation

stops.name: Moscow, leaving the league
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the break with KVN; no month recorded, defaulted to January. The specific grievances are given in Zelenskyy's own later public accounts and in Shuster, which is testimony rather than documentation; the refusal of the buyout offer is attested.
stops.campa: He walks out of KVN. By his own later account the reasons stack up: fees withheld, material struck before broadcast, and an antisemitic remark from a Russian producer that he does not forget. He is offered a large sum to dissolve Kvartal 95 and return inside the league on its terms, and he turns it down. It is a commercial decision taken at twenty-five by a comedian with no other platform, and it costs him the largest stage in the Russian-language world. He goes to Kyiv instead and builds another one.
suggested_refs: Zelenskyy's public accounts of the break with KVN's Russian management

stops.name: Kyiv, the studio founded
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month. The studio's exact street address at founding is not confirmed; central Kyiv coordinates are used. A supplied research note dating the founding to September 1998 is rejected: it contradicts the same note's own chronology and is not attested anywhere reachable.
stops.campa: In September, with Serhiy and Borys Shefir and the rest of the troupe, he registers Kvartal 95 as a production company in Kyiv. It is no longer an act taking bookings. It writes, films, produces and sells; inside two years it is supplying prime-time comedy to a national channel, and by the end of the decade it is making sitcoms and feature films. Twelve years on it will make a series about a schoolteacher elected president of Ukraine by accident. Zelenskyy is twenty-five and his name is on the papers.
suggested_refs: Kvartal 95 Studio, founded September 2003 with Serhiy and Borys Shefir

stops.name: Kryvyi Rih, marrying Olena Kiyashko
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to place and day. The marriage year is attested; the date of 6 September and the hometown ceremony are widely repeated in the Ukrainian press but were not verified against a civil record in this pass. Olena's remark about learning of the candidacy from television is reported in interviews and is treated here as reconstruction.
stops.campa: He marries Olena Kiyashko, born in the same city eleven days after him, schooled in the same quarter, an architect by training who has been writing scripts for Kvartal 95. She goes on writing them. Their daughter Oleksandra is born the following July and a son, Kyrylo, in January 2013. Olena will say afterwards that she learned her husband was running for president the same way the rest of the country learned it, from the television, on the last night of the year.
suggested_refs: Olena Zelenska, screenwriter for Kvartal 95 and later First Lady of Ukraine
sources: Ukrainian biographical retrospectives on the Zelenskyy family

stops.name: Kyiv, Evening Kvartal goes out to the whole country
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year. The broadcaster is Inter, not 1+1: the studio moved its operations to Inter in 2005 and the 1+1 association belongs to the later period. The Inter studio's precise address is unconfirmed and the pin is central Kyiv. An audience-share figure above eighty-five percent circulates in the trade press and is not verified here.
stops.campa: Kvartal 95 moves its work to the Inter channel and launches Vecherniy Kvartal, a sketch show that goes out to the whole country and takes apart, week by week, the people who govern it. Oligarchs, deputies, prime ministers and presidents are played by men who grew up in a mining town and are very hard to embarrass. It becomes the most watched entertainment programme in Ukraine and stays there for a decade, by which time there is nowhere in the country he is not recognised. In 2006 he also wins the first season of the Ukrainian Dancing with the Stars.
suggested_refs: Vecherniy Kvartal on Inter, from 2005

stops.name: Moscow, the New Year on Russia-1
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The channel is Russia-1 with Maxim Galkin, not Channel One; a supplied research note naming Channel One is rejected. A separate 2011 Russian engagement was the X Factor. Coordinates are central Moscow; the studio is not identified.
stops.campa: By now he is a working star of Russian television as well as Ukrainian: Napoleon in a Russian costume comedy in 2012, a leading man in romantic films that sell in both markets, co-writer and star of 8 First Dates. Eight hundred kilometres south-west of Moscow the Maidan has been occupied for six weeks, and people will be shot dead on Instytutska Street before February is out. On the last night of 2013 he presents the New Year's Eve show on Russia-1 beside the Russian comedian Maxim Galkin, to the largest audience either country assembles all year.
suggested_refs: The Russia-1 New Year's Eve broadcast, 31 December 2013

stops.name: Donbas, playing for the soldiers
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for both the closure of the Moscow office and the frontline tours; individual towns on the tour route are not documented and the pin is the Sloviansk and Kramatorsk area of the Donbas front. The month is set to June to order the segment.
stops.campa: Russia takes Crimea in March and the war in the east opens in April. Kvartal 95 closes its Moscow office, and the Russian market, which is most of the studio's money, closes with it. Zelenskyy takes the troupe east instead. They perform for Ukrainian soldiers inside artillery range, on flatbed stages, in canteens, in halls with the windows taped against blast. He gives money to the army and says publicly that he has. The jokes are largely the jokes they played in Moscow, delivered now to men who have been on the line since spring.
suggested_refs: Kvartal 95's wartime tours of the Donbas, 2014 to 2015
sources: Ukrainian press coverage of the 2014-2015 frontline tours

stops.name: Kyiv, Servant of the People
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year of first broadcast; the exact premiere date is not carried in the pool and the month is set to October. Filmed in and around Kyiv; the pin is the studio's central Kyiv location.
stops.campa: Kvartal 95 films and airs Sluha Narodu. Zelenskyy plays Vasyl Holoborodko, a history teacher recorded by a pupil while swearing about corruption in a staff room, who wakes to find the video everywhere and himself elected president of Ukraine. For four years Ukrainians watch a man with Zelenskyy's face refuse the motorcade and the bribe and the official residence, and govern from a bicycle and a two-room flat, and it is the most detailed picture of an honest Ukrainian president anyone has. The show runs three seasons.
suggested_refs: Sluha Narodu (Servant of the People), Kvartal 95, three seasons from 2015
sources: Series production credits; international press coverage

stops.name: Kyiv, a party named after a television show
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month. The pin is the studio's central Kyiv location rather than the registration office, which is not identified in the pool.
stops.campa: In March, members of Kvartal 95 register a political party. They call it Servant of the People, which is the name of the television programme their employer stars in. No candidate is announced, no manifesto is published, no branch offices open. For nine months the party exists as a name held in reserve, a legal shell with a title borrowed from fiction. That same year Zelenskyy takes his first film role performed in Ukrainian rather than Russian, in Me. You. He. She.
suggested_refs: The registration of the Servant of the People party, March 2018

stops.name: Kyiv, the candidacy announced at midnight
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Coordinates are approximate to the 1+1 broadcaster's Kyiv facility; the exact studio address is not confirmed in the pool.
stops.campa: On the last night of the year, in the slot Ukrainian television reserves for the president's address to the nation, the 1+1 channel broadcasts Zelenskyy instead. He announces that he is running. Petro Poroshenko's own recorded address goes out afterwards, pushed past midnight in some regions. The candidacy is launched the way a new season is launched, on the one night when the whole country is in front of a television with a glass in its hand. There is no campaign headquarters, no policy platform, and almost no rallies.
suggested_refs: The 1+1 New Year's Eve broadcast of 31 December 2018
sources: Contemporary Ukrainian and international press coverage

stops.name: Olimpiyskiy stadium, the debate in the centre circle
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Zelenskyy's line about being the verdict of the people rather than a politician is a paraphrase from press summaries, not a verbatim transcript, and is written as paraphrase here.
stops.campa: He has taken about thirty percent in the first round to Poroshenko's sixteen. He will not debate in a studio; he demands the national stadium, and the incumbent agrees. Tens of thousands fill the Olimpiyskiy on a Friday evening to watch two men on separate podiums in the centre circle with their own supporters massed behind each of them. Both submit to a public drug test beforehand, at Zelenskyy's insistence. Poroshenko argues Ukraine's place in Europe. Zelenskyy argues that he is not a politician at all but the country's verdict on the man opposite.
suggested_refs: The Olimpiyskiy stadium debate of 19 April 2019, an unprecedented format in Ukrainian politics
sources: BBC, Reuters and AP coverage of the April 2019 debate

stops.name: Parkovy Centre, seventy-three percent
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the result; the venue of the victory speech is reconstruction from election-night press coverage. His remark that everything is possible is a paraphrase of widely reported remarks, not a verified transcript.
stops.campa: The exit polls come in at three to one and the count confirms them: about seventy-three percent against twenty-four, the widest margin in the history of independent Ukraine, carried in every region but one. He comes out to his campaign staff at the Parkovy centre above the Dnipro. He is forty-one, he has never held any office, he has no faction in parliament and no ministers, and his party has no deputies at all. To the other post-Soviet states watching the count, he says that everything is possible.
suggested_refs: The Ukrainian presidential runoff of 21 April 2019 and its regional breakdown

stops.name: Verkhovna Rada, the oath and the dissolution
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Coordinates corrected to the Verkhovna Rada building at 5 Hrushevsky Street; a figure of 30.5326 circulating in the research pool places the point about three hundred metres west of the chamber. The remark about portraits is a paraphrase of widely reported inaugural remarks.
stops.campa: He takes the oath in the chamber on Hrushevsky Street, hand on the Peresopnytsia Gospel and the constitution, and becomes the sixth president of Ukraine and the first Jewish one. With Volodymyr Groysman still prime minister, Ukraine is briefly the only country on earth besides Israel with a Jew as both head of state and head of government. Then he dissolves the parliament that has just sworn him in and calls elections for July. He tells the deputies not to hang his portrait in their offices and to hang photographs of their children instead.
suggested_refs: The inauguration of 20 May 2019 and the same-day dissolution of the Rada
sources: Official presidential records; international press coverage

stops.name: Verkhovna Rada, the immunity stripped
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The vote tally is not carried in the pool and no number is stated here.
stops.campa: The new parliament, three quarters of it his own party and much of it composed of people who have never held office in their lives, convenes and votes to strip its own members of the legal immunity from prosecution that Ukrainian deputies have enjoyed since independence. It was the centrepiece of the campaign. It passes in a single sitting. The press names the chamber the turbo-regime, for the speed at which it passes whatever is put in front of it. Whether that is praise is not settled then and is not settled later.
suggested_refs: The September 2019 bill removing parliamentary immunity in Ukraine

stops.name: Elysee Palace, face to face with Putin
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Macron hosts the Normandy Format at the Elysee: France, Germany, Russia and Ukraine in one room for the first time in three years. Zelenskyy, seven months in office and elected on a promise to end the war in the Donbas, meets Vladimir Putin face to face. They agree a prisoner exchange and a ceasefire along the contact line. The ceasefire does not hold. Asked afterwards what he has achieved, Zelenskyy says that he did not manage to solve every question and that nobody in the room had expected him to.
suggested_refs: The Normandy Format summit of 9 December 2019, Paris
sources: International press coverage of the December 2019 Paris summit

stops.name: Yad Vashem, the number said out loud
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the address at the World Holocaust Forum. The specific family losses are drawn from Zelenskyy's own repeated public accounts.
stops.campa: He speaks at the World Holocaust Forum on the Mount of Remembrance, seventy-five years after the gates of Auschwitz were opened. Roughly one and a half million Jews were murdered on Ukrainian ground, and he is the president of the state that ground belongs to, saying the number out loud in Jerusalem to a hall of presidents and kings. He speaks also as a man whose own family did not come through it whole: three of his grandfather's brothers killed, the grandfather the only one of four sons to live, and he lived in a Soviet uniform.
suggested_refs: The Fifth World Holocaust Forum, Yad Vashem, January 2020

stops.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau, the seventy-fifth anniversary
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Four days later he is at the camp itself for the official liberation ceremony, among the survivors and the heads of state under the shelter erected over the gate at Birkenau. Survivor after survivor takes the microphone and makes the same argument: that all of it began in speech, in a state's decision about which people counted as people, and that the decision was popular long before it was lethal. The heads of state hear it in January 2020 as history; twenty-five months on, Russian shells fall beside the Babyn Yar memorial in Kyiv. Zelenskyy lays a wreath.
suggested_refs: The 75th anniversary liberation ceremony at Auschwitz-Birkenau, 27 January 2020
sources: International press coverage of the January 2020 Auschwitz ceremony

stops.name: Chernobyl, the arch and the empty town
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: On the thirty-fifth anniversary he walks the exclusion zone: the sealed reactor under its steel arch, the abandoned school and the drained swimming pool of Pripyat, the memorial to the liquidators who were sent in and told very little about what they were being sent into. He lays flowers. He signs a decree on developing the zone and talks about making it a place people travel to rather than a place they are kept out of. Ten months later Russian armour will drive through it on the road from Belarus and dig trenches in the contaminated forest.
suggested_refs: The New Safe Confinement over Reactor No. 4 and the town of Pripyat
sources: International coverage of the 2021 Chernobyl anniversary

stops.name: Bayerischer Hof, Munich, the guarantees of 1994
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The characterisation of advice against the trip is drawn from contemporary reporting rather than a document.
stops.campa: Five days before the invasion he flies to Munich, over the objection of everyone who tells him not to leave the country with Russian divisions massed on three borders. He tells the Security Conference that Ukraine surrendered the third largest nuclear arsenal on earth in 1994 in exchange for written guarantees, that the guarantees are not being honoured, and that he would like to know what the whole security architecture is for if not for this. Ukraine will defend itself with partners or without them, he says. Then he flies home.
suggested_refs: The Budapest Memorandum of 1994 and Ukraine's nuclear disarmament
sources: International press coverage of the February 2022 conference

stops.name: Kyiv, the address sent to Russia
stops.date_confidence: attested. Wikisource and the NBC News transcript behind it both date the address 24 February 2022; it was recorded late on the twenty-third and aired in the small hours of the twenty-fourth, roughly an hour before the invasion began. Coordinates are the Office of the President at 11 Bankova Street; the recording location is not separately documented.
stops.campa: In the small hours, with the invasion an hour off and every intelligence service on earth saying so, he records an address and sends it across the border. He speaks in Russian, which is his own first language, and tells the Russian public that he is speaking not as a president but as a citizen of Ukraine. He reads out the names of Ukrainian towns to an audience told nightly that the country is an invention. He notes inside the speech itself that nobody in Russia will understand what the names mean. Nothing stops. Around five in the morning the missiles arrive.
stops.quote: I am addressing you not as a president, I am addressing you as a citizen of Ukraine.
stops.quote_source: Video address to the people of Russia, broadcast in Russian, 24 February 2022 (Wikisource, from the NBC News full transcript)
suggested_refs: The full transcript of the 24 February 2022 address to the Russian people
sources: Wikipedia, 'Timeline of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine'

stops.name: Mariinskyi Palace, we are all here
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The location is contested: the research pool placed the video on Bankova Street, but Wikipedia places it outside the Mariinskyi Palace, and the Mariinskyi coordinates are used here. The wording is paraphrased in the campa rather than quoted, since no verbatim English transcript is carried in the pool.
stops.campa: Russian columns are in the northern suburbs and Russian state media is reporting that the president has fled to Lviv, or to Poland, or to a bunker abroad. He walks out into the dark of the government quarter with Andriy Yermak, Denys Shmyhal, Mykhailo Podolyak and David Arakhamia, holds a phone out at arm's length, and names each man standing beside him. The head of the office is here. The prime minister is here. The president is here. The video runs forty-two seconds, shot on the phone in his own hand, in the street, in the dark.
suggested_refs: The 'we are all here' video of 25 February 2022, filmed outside the Mariinskyi Palace
sources: Wikipedia, 'Speeches by Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the Russian invasion of Ukraine'
Video archived by international press, 25 February 2022

stops.name: The bunker under the government compound, ammunition and not a ride
stops.date_confidence: attested, after a four-year dispute. First reported by James LaPorta for AP at 04:04 UTC on 26 February 2022, sourced to a senior American intelligence official with direct knowledge; AP's full rendering is 'The fight is here; I need ammunition, not a ride.' The Washington Post Fact Checker could not confirm it in March 2022 and Biden administration officials denied it and demanded a retraction AP refused. Zelenskyy confirmed the line himself in February 2023 to Dmytro Komarov and again on 24 February 2026 in his own voice on the presidency's official site, naming Biden as the caller and the bunker as the room.
stops.campa: On the third day of the war, in the shelter under the government compound, an offer reaches him from Washington: there is a threat, you need to leave Ukraine urgently, we are ready to help with that. Joseph Biden is on the line. Zelenskyy answers that what he needs is ammunition, not a ride. The Associated Press has the sentence within hours from an American official; the White House denies it and demands a retraction that never comes; fact-checkers file it for years under unconfirmed. Four years later he stands in the same room and says it into a camera himself.
stops.quote: I need ammunition, not a ride.
stops.quote_source: Reported by James LaPorta, Associated Press, 26 February 2022; confirmed by Zelenskyy in February 2023 and again on 24 February 2026
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'I need ammunition, not a ride', for the full provenance chain
sources: president.gov.ua, address on the fourth anniversary, 24 February 2026

stops.name: Kyiv, the Heroes of Snake Island
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the announcement; the premise of the announcement was wrong. Zelenskyy announced posthumous Hero of Ukraine titles for the thirteen Snake Island border guards, but the Ukrainian Navy confirmed on 28 February 2022 that all of them were alive and had been captured by the Russian Navy. The radio operator was released on 30 March 2022 and decorated. This stop is placed at Zelenskyy's own pin in Kyiv, not on Snake Island, where he never was.
stops.campa: On the first morning a Russian cruiser demands the surrender of the garrison on Snake Island in the Black Sea, and the answer, caught on the radio and released within hours, is an obscenity. The country needs it. Zelenskyy announces that the thirteen border guards have been killed and names each of them a Hero of Ukraine. Days later the navy establishes that they are alive and in Russian custody. The operator who swore at the cruiser is released at the end of March and is decorated by Zelenskyy in person.
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'Attack on Snake Island', for the survival and release of the border guards
sources: Wikipedia, 'Timeline of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine'

segments.name: The Voice Sent Where the Body Cannot Go

stops.name: Kyiv, Brussels and the Commons addressed by video
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for both addresses (European Parliament 1 March, UK Parliament 8 March), both delivered by video link from Ukraine. The stop is pinned in Kyiv, where Zelenskyy actually was, rather than at the chambers, which he did not enter. The Shevchenko Day observance of 9 March is reconstruction from the standing practice of the Ukrainian presidency and general reporting; it was not verified against president.gov.ua in this pass.
stops.campa: He cannot leave the country, so the country's case travels without him. On the first of March he asks the European Parliament in Brussels to admit Ukraine to the Union without delay, and the interpreter breaks down mid-sentence on the live feed. On the eighth he tells the House of Commons that the question now is to be or not to be, and that Ukraine will fight in the forests, the fields, the shores and the streets. On the ninth, the birthday of Taras Shevchenko, he marks the poet's anniversary from the same rooms, in the middle of a siege.
suggested_refs: European Parliament records, 1 March 2022
Hansard, UK Parliament, 8 March 2022
Taras Shevchenko Day, 9 March, in Ukrainian presidential practice
sources: International press coverage of the March 2022 addresses

stops.name: Kyiv, Ottawa and the Bundestag addressed by video
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for both addresses (Canadian Parliament 15 March, Bundestag 17 March), both by video link from Ukraine. Pinned in Kyiv rather than at the chambers. The rhetorical specifics of each speech are drawn from the parliamentary records and contemporary coverage rather than from a verbatim transcript carried in this pool.
stops.campa: On the fifteenth he asks the Canadian parliament to close the sky over Ukraine and asks the members to picture the tower over Toronto with missiles coming at it. On the seventeenth he tells the Bundestag that a wall has gone up across Europe again, that Germany is standing on the far side of it, that the pipeline was one of its stones, and that history will read what they choose this month. The chamber gives him a standing ovation and then returns to its order of business. Berlin sends helmets in March and heavy weapons much later.
suggested_refs: Canadian Parliament records, 15 March 2022
Bundestag records, 17 March 2022

stops.name: Kyiv, the Knesset and Golda Meir's sentence
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; delivered by video link from Ukraine to the chamber in Jerusalem. Pinned in Kyiv. The Golda Meir line is quoted by Zelenskyy inside his own address; the words are hers, cited by him, not his coinage.
stops.campa: He addresses Israel's parliament from Kyiv and reaches, in front of it, for Golda Meir, who was born in Kyiv: we intend to remain alive, our neighbours want to see us dead. He tells the members that eighty years ago Ukrainians rescued Jews, and that the people of Israel now have such a choice in front of them. He compares the invasion to the Final Solution, and members of the Knesset object publicly and immediately to the comparison. The government goes on declining to send weapons and goes on offering to mediate.
stops.quote: People of Israel, now you have such a choice.
stops.quote_source: Speech to the Knesset by video link, 20 March 2022 (Wikisource English transcript)
suggested_refs: Wikisource, 'Speech by President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Knesset'
sources: International press coverage, including Israeli criticism of the Holocaust comparison

stops.name: Bucha, the road past the bodies
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the visit and for the address delivered the same night.
stops.campa: The Russians withdraw from the north on the thirtieth of March. Five days later he walks through Bucha in body armour, past cars burned with people still inside them, past bodies lying where they were shot in the street, past the trench dug beside the church of Saint Andrew where the town has been putting its dead. He tells the press pool that it is very difficult to negotiate when you see what they did here. That night he addresses the nation and opens without a greeting, which is not how he opens addresses.
stops.quote: Concentrated evil has come to our land. Murderers. Torturers. Rapists. Looters.
stops.quote_source: Address to the nation following the Bucha massacre, 4 April 2022 (Wikisource English transcript)
suggested_refs: Wikisource, 'Address to the nation by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy following the Bucha Massacre'
sources: International press pool coverage of the 4 April 2022 visit

stops.name: Irpin, the ruined street shown to three leaders
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Macron, Scholz and Draghi arrive in Kyiv together, having spent four months being told by their own newspapers that they are too slow, and Zelenskyy takes them twenty kilometres north-west to Irpin. They walk a street of gutted apartment blocks and burned cars where the Russian advance on the capital was stopped in March. In Irpin the three of them say the word candidate out loud: Ukraine should have candidate status for the European Union. The European Council grants it seven days afterwards, on the twenty-third of June.
suggested_refs: The joint Kyiv and Irpin visit of Macron, Scholz and Draghi, 16 June 2022
sources: International press coverage of the 16 June 2022 visit

stops.name: Izium, the flag raised the day before the forest
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, and the sequence matters. Zelenskyy visited Izium on 14 September 2022; the mass burial site in the pine forest was found on 15 September and exhumations began on 16 September. A supplied research note describing him as arriving days after exhumations began inverts the causality and is corrected here.
stops.campa: The Kharkiv counteroffensive takes back thousands of square kilometres in a week, and Izium with them. Zelenskyy arrives on the fourteenth, stands with soldiers while the flag goes up over the wrecked administration building, and does not stay long; the town is mined and the front is not far. The next day, in the pine forest at the edge of Izium, investigators find the burial ground: hundreds of graves, most of them marked with nothing but a number on a wooden cross. He is not there when they open it.
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'Izium mass graves', for the discovery of 15 September and the exhumations from 16 September
sources: International press coverage of the September 2022 Izium visit and exhumations

stops.name: Kherson, Freedom Square
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. His remark about the beginning of the end is a paraphrase of widely reported remarks rather than a verified transcript.
stops.campa: Russian forces cross to the left bank of the Dnipro on the eleventh, blowing the Antonivskyi bridge behind them. Three days later he is standing in Freedom Square in the middle of Kherson, the one regional capital Russia had taken and held, in a crowd that has spent eight and a half months under occupation and is still counting its missing. The flag goes up. The anthem is sung by people who could have been arrested that summer for singing it. He says this is the beginning of the end of the war.
suggested_refs: The liberation of Kherson, 11 November 2022, and the presidential visit of the fourteenth
sources: International press coverage of the 14 November 2022 Kherson visit

stops.name: Bakhmut, the flag the soldiers sign
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He goes east to Bakhmut, where the front has settled into a battle of pure attrition over a town of seventy thousand that is being reduced to brick dust and will go on being reduced for another five months. He hands out medals in a building with the windows blown out and the ceiling down at one end. The soldiers give him a Ukrainian flag they have signed, name by name. He takes it, gets into a car, rides overnight by rail to the Polish border, and boards an American aircraft to Washington with the flag folded in his hands.
suggested_refs: The battle of Bakhmut, and the signed flag carried to the United States Congress
sources: International press coverage of the December 2022 Bakhmut visit

stops.name: United States Capitol, the first journey out
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Pedantically it was a joint meeting of Congress, not a joint session; a supplied research note tagging this as reconstruction is rejected, the trip of 21-22 December 2022 being fully documented. A separate address to Congress by video took place on 16 March 2022.
stops.campa: It is his first journey outside Ukraine in three hundred days. He walks into the chamber in an olive fleece and army boots, hands the signed Bakhmut flag to the Speaker and the Vice President, and delivers the address in English, a language he learned as a grown man. He tells them the American money is not charity but an investment in global security and in democracy, and that Ukraine is alive and kicking. At the White House the same day Joseph Biden pledges a Patriot air defence battery, the first.
stops.quote: The Russian tyranny has lost control over us. And it will never influence our minds again.
stops.quote_source: Address to the United States Congress, 21 December 2022 (English transcript, Wikisource)
suggested_refs: Wikisource, 'Address by President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy to the US Congress'
The Bakhmut flag displayed at the Capitol
sources: Wikipedia, 'List of international presidential trips made by Volodymyr Zelenskyy'

stops.name: Westminster Hall, the pilot's helmet
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the London visit and for the same-day Paris meeting with Macron and Scholz; the Brussels leg followed on 9 February. The inscription on the helmet is reported in contemporary coverage.
stops.campa: Eleven months after addressing the Commons down a video link he arrives at Westminster in person, unannounced until that morning, in the same olive green he has worn since February. He presents the helmet of a Ukrainian fighter pilot, inscribed with a line asking for wings to protect the freedom Ukraine already has, and asks for combat aircraft. Both Houses stand. He is promised pilot training and no jets. The same evening he is at the Elysee with Macron and Scholz, and the next day in Brussels, asking three capitals in two days for the same thing.
suggested_refs: UK Parliament records of the address of 8 February 2023
sources: International press coverage of the February 2023 European trip

stops.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, the cenotaph and the dome
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He flies to Japan for the G7 and goes to the Peace Memorial Park: the museum, the cenotaph, the gutted dome left standing exactly as the blast left it. He lays a wreath and meets survivors. He says the photographs of Hiroshima in 1945 look to him like Bakhmut looks now, and adds the part that matters to him, which is that Hiroshima was rebuilt. Then he sits down with the leaders of the seven richest democracies and with the prime minister of India, and asks again for aircraft.
suggested_refs: The Genbaku Dome and the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum
sources: International press coverage of the May 2023 Hiroshima visit

stops.name: Litexpo, Vilnius, the summit that sets no date
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the summit ran 11-12 July 2023. Coordinates corrected to the Litexpo halls on Laisves prospektas; a figure of 54.6863 / 25.2564 circulating in the research pool sits about two and a half kilometres north-east, in the city rather than at the venue.
stops.campa: Before he has landed he posts that it is absurd for the alliance to set no timeframe at all, neither for an invitation nor for membership, and that an undefined condition looks to him like a bargaining chip in negotiations with Russia. The communique offers a pathway and no date. He has said in public what heads of government normally say in corridors, is told privately that this is not how it is done, and by the second day is thanking the members for a new Ukraine-NATO Council and a long-term aid package.
suggested_refs: The Vilnius Summit Communique of 11 July 2023 and its language on Ukrainian membership
sources: International press coverage of the July 2023 Vilnius summit

stops.name: United Nations General Assembly, the argument put to the small states
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: He comes to New York and speaks in the General Assembly hall in person for the first time as a wartime president. He describes a state that has weaponised food, energy, children and a working nuclear power plant, and he puts the case less to the great powers than to the small ones in the room: that a guarantee which goes unanswered once is worth nothing to any of them afterwards, whatever it says on paper. Russia holds a seat in the same building with a veto attached to it.
suggested_refs: UN General Assembly records, 78th session, 19 September 2023

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires, at Milei's handover
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from the corpus Casa Rosada pin used in javier_milei.journey.json and the Peronist files, which is the standing anchor for the building rather than the generic Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: He flies to Buenos Aires, twenty-two months into an invasion, to stand among the foreign guests at the swearing-in of Javier Milei. Milei has spent the campaign promising alignment with the United States and Israel and a break with Moscow and Beijing, and Zelenskyy has come to collect on it in person, in a hemisphere where the war is a distant European quarrel and Russian grain and fertiliser are not distant at all. The two men meet at the Casa Rosada during the handover. It is the furthest from Kyiv he travels in the whole war.
suggested_refs: The Argentine presidential inauguration of 10 December 2023
sources: International press coverage of the December 2023 inauguration

stops.name: The White House, the Oval Office on camera
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and recorded on video in its entirety.
stops.campa: He returns to the Oval Office to sign a minerals agreement and is confronted on camera instead. Donald Trump and JD Vance tell him he is not being grateful, that he is gambling with world war three, that he has no cards. A reporter asks him why he is not wearing a suit. He answers that he will wear one when the war is over, and perhaps one like the questioner's, and perhaps a better one. The lunch is cancelled, the agreement is not signed that day, and he is out of the building early.
suggested_refs: The olive-green wartime clothing adopted in February 2022 and its reading in Washington three years later
sources: Widely reported coverage of the 28 February 2025 Oval Office meeting

stops.name: The bunker under the government compound, four years on
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the address is published in his own voice on president.gov.ua. His term expired under the ordinary five-year cycle in May 2024 and elections cannot be held while martial law is in force; this is stated as the legal position, not as a judgement on it.
stops.campa: Four years to the day, he films the anniversary address in the shelter under the government compound where the war began for him, and walks the camera to the exact spot. His term ran out in May 2024 under the ordinary five-year cycle, and elections cannot be held while martial law is in force, so he is still president. The argument he makes about the room is the argument he made on the second night: if the capital falls and the leader has gone, there is no state left for anyone to come back to.
stops.quote: Here I spoke with President Biden, and it was right here that I heard: Volodymyr, there is a threat. You need to leave Ukraine urgently. We are ready to help with that. And here I replied that I need ammunition, not a ride.
stops.quote_source: Address on the fourth anniversary of the full-scale invasion, filmed in the government bunker, 24 February 2026 (president.gov.ua, English text)
suggested_refs: president.gov.ua, address of 24 February 2026, for the bunker and the Biden call
sources: Wikipedia, 'I need ammunition, not a ride'
